free_tier.stated: We provide grants between 5.000 and 50.000 euro — with the possibility to scale them up if there is proven potential.

chaining: Individuals are eligible: 'In principle anyone can apply: individuals, research organisations, non-profits, public institutions, companies of any size and type, etc.' Follow-up funding can be applied for.
limits_note: Must be technical development, released under an open licence, and no AI-generated proposals ('We are not interested in AI-generated projects or proposals'). EU-supported funds require a European dimension - a non-EU applicant must pick a fund whose eligibility section does not impose it. Money arrives against a contract, so a bank account and a legal entity are needed.
reliability_note: Realistic size: a EUR 50k grant buys roughly 12-25 TB-months at Hetzner-class pricing, or funds an engineer - it does not buy 20 TB for five years. Treat grants as funding the software around the storage, not the storage.
confidence_note: We provide grants between 5.000 and 50.000 euro — with the possibility to scale them up if there is proven potential.

Money arrives against a contract, so a bank account and a legal entity are needed.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Explicitly individual-eligible: 'In principle anyone can apply: individuals, research organisations, non-profits, public institutions, companies of any size and type'. A second grant can follow a first. Funds open at proposal time: Restack, CodeSupply, Other/open call.
extras.agent_focus: Bulk data programmes that pay for your storage. Two halves: (1) institutional/gov repositories and cloud open-data sponsorships, judged as free byte pools; (2) research grants that could fund storage for an unaffiliated individual. Revisited AWS ODS, Google Cloud public datasets, Source Cooperative. Central question for each: what is the unit of quota (account / record / dataset / collection / project), because that unit is the multiplier.
